rows.note: Responses are produced by minimal-API Results (JSON with charset, Results.File with an explicit media type), problem details and WriteAsJsonAsync; SecurityHeadersMiddleware adds nosniff to every response. No test asserts Content-Type across all endpoints; only the quote PDF download is checked (attachment + nosniff).

Ingress has allowInsecure=false, so Container Apps redirects plain HTTP to HTTPS for every path including /api (the app has no UseHttpsRedirection of its own, and API clients are not told to fail instead). app.UseHsts() is called with framework defaults (30 days, no includeSubDomains), contradicting docs/06-security.md:41 (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains).
rows.fix: Add services.AddHsts(o => { o.MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromDays(365); o.IncludeSubDomains = true; }) in Program.cs; optionally decide in infra whether /api should refuse instead of redirect. Add an integration test on the Strict-Transport-Security header.

rows.note: ForwardedHeaders trusts X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Host from any sender (KnownIPNetworks and KnownProxies cleared) and AllowedHosts is "*". Behind Container Apps ingress the proxy appends the real client IP (ForwardLimit 1 takes the right-most value), but the X-Forwarded-Host a client sends is not shown to be stripped, and Request.Host feeds the OIDC redirect_uri. Entra rejects unregistered reply URLs, so impact is limited. No test.
rows.fix: Drop ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedHost (or pin AllowedHosts to the application FQDN via Bicep) and test that a forged X-Forwarded-Host does not change Request.Host.

rows.note: Message framing is delegated to Kestrel behind the Azure Container Apps (Envoy) ingress; Kestrel rejects conflicting Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding by default and the repo changes no Kestrel limits or HTTP options. The behaviour of the ingress layer cannot be verified from the repo and there is no request-smuggling test.
rows.fix: Include request-smuggling probes (CL.TE / TE.CL) against the test environment ingress in the independent test; no code change expected.

rows.note: No GraphQL, OData or other client-supplied query/expression language exists (verified by search of src/ and csproj files). List endpoints take fixed filters and a keyset limit clamped by KeysetCursor.ClampLimit.
No GraphQL endpoint exists in the application; the only machine-readable schema endpoint is the OpenAPI document mapped at Program.cs:214 (its exposure is a V13 question, not assessed here).
The web host has no WebSocket/SignalR endpoint (no UseWebSockets, MapHub or SignalR package found in src/); the request pipeline at Program.cs:192-241 maps only HTTP endpoints.
No WebSocket handshake exists in the application (see V4.4.1).
No WebSocket channel; the standard cookie session is the only session mechanism.
No WebSocket channel, so no dedicated WebSocket tokens.

The only inputs that resemble uploads are four CSV text bodies (organization migration, NCE price sheet, subscription import, MS billing import). docs/06-security.md:45 describes an upload allow-list, a 25 MB limit, signature checks and Defender for Storage that do not exist in code or infra; the actual formats, maximum size (Kestrel default ~30 MB) and the 5000-row migration cap are not documented per endpoint.
rows.fix: Replace the generic upload sentence in docs/06-security.md with a table of the four CSV endpoints (accepted format, encoding, max bytes, max rows, permission) and set explicit limits (see F-G2-05).

rows.note: No size limit is configured anywhere (no MaxRequestBodySize or RequestSizeLimit found); only the Kestrel default (~28.6 MB) applies. The import handlers buffer the entire body (MemoryStream / StreamReader.ReadToEnd) and parse it into List<List<string>> before any row cap (MigrationImport.MaxRows=5000 is checked after parsing; the licensing and price-sheet imports have no row cap). Callers need LicensingManage / FinanceCostRead / CustomersDelete, and only the migration and export endpoints have extra rate limits (global 300 req/min applies to the rest).
rows.fix: Set [RequestSizeLimit]/IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature (e.g. 5 MB) on the four import endpoints, read with a bounded stream, cap rows before building the table, and put the licensing and price-sheet imports under the Migration rate-limit policy.

rows.note: Imports take a raw request body: no file name, extension or Content-Type is checked (any media type is accepted). Content is validated structurally: the migration import decodes with an encoding check, requires a header with a name column and rejects bad rows with reasons, and CsvTable reports ragged rows and unterminated quotes; the licensing and price-sheet parsers reject unknown shapes. Nothing is stored as a file.
rows.fix: Require Content-Type text/csv or text/plain on the four import endpoints and reject binary content (NUL bytes) before parsing.

rows.note: The application accepts no compressed files or archives: the only file-like inputs are plain-text CSV bodies and there is no ZipArchive/GZipStream/request-decompression code in src/ (verified by search). The XLSX organization export is generated, never read back.

No user-supplied file lands in a web-served folder: UseStaticFiles serves only the built SPA in wwwroot; generated PDFs and manifests go to the private Blob container (production refuses the folder store, DocumentStores.cs:47) or a folder outside wwwroot in development. Stored objects are only ever returned as bytes through authorised API endpoints, never executed.

Storage keys are built from internal GUIDs (quotes/{rootId}/{quoteId}/{documentId}.pdf) and guarded by DocumentKeys.Guard (allow-list of characters, no "..", no leading slash, <=512); the file store additionally checks the resolved path stays under the root. A unit theory covers ../, absolute and spaced keys. No user file name is used in any path.

Download file names are server-generated (quote number + version, timestamped export name) and never taken from request parameters; Results.File sets Content-Disposition (attachment, asserted by the quote document integration test).

Names are built from server-controlled values (quote numbers, dates); Results.File serialises the name through ContentDispositionHeaderValue (RFC 6266 filename/filename*). Residual: the quote Number format itself is assumed to be server-generated; no test feeds hostile characters through it.

No file from an untrusted source is stored or served: imports are parsed in memory and only a SHA-256 and row results are kept; the document store holds only server-generated PDFs/JSON. (docs/06-security.md:45 nevertheless promises Defender for Storage; infra contains no Defender setting - see V5.1.1.)

Credential attacks are delegated to Entra (CA, MFA, Smart Lockout) and SEC-AUTH-01/02 say so, but the documentation does not state which anti-automation controls apply to the CRM entry points (/bff/login, /signin-oidc, dev sign-in) and the global rate limiter only covers /api, not /bff. The delegation itself is unproven in this repo.
rows.fix: Add a short "authentication abuse controls" paragraph to docs/06-security.md: Entra Smart Lockout/CA own credential guessing; /bff/* is not rate limited by design (or add a limiter on /bff/login).

rows.note: The CRM stores and verifies no passwords: users are created only from Entra identities (UserProvisioning), so no context-specific password word list applies. Entra password protection is a tenant setting.

Pathways are: Entra OIDC cookie session, Entra bearer for /api/v1/bi, and the development sign-in (Development only). Each is described (SEC-AUTH-*, SEC-AZ-04c, ADR-019 item 7) but there is no single list that ties pathway to controls.
rows.fix: Add an "authentication pathways" table to docs/06-security.md (cookie/OIDC, BI bearer, dev sign-in, worker managed identity) with their controls.

rows.note: The CRM has no local passwords (minimum length is therefore an Entra tenant concern): the only sign-in is OIDC code+PKCE to Entra (AuthenticationSetup.cs:36-70); the development sign-in is refused outside the Development environment (AuthenticationSetup.cs:30, ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production in 0:102) and has no password.

The CRM has no local passwords (breached-password check is therefore an Entra tenant concern): the only sign-in is OIDC code+PKCE to Entra (AuthenticationSetup.cs:36-70); the development sign-in is refused outside the Development environment (AuthenticationSetup.cs:30, ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production in 0:102) and has no password.

Brute-force and credential-stuffing protection exists only in Entra (Smart Lockout, Conditional Access, MFA); the application never receives credentials. Configuration of those controls in the real tenant cannot be verified from the repo.

No default accounts exist in production: the dev-* identities are created only by /bff/dev-login, which requires Auth:Mode=Development AND IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment (otherwise 404, covered in the integration host), startup throws if Mode=Development outside Development, and the SQL server is Entra-only (azureADOnlyAuthentication). The local sa password in appsettings.Development.json belongs to a developer container. The startup throw itself has no unit test.
MFA is a Conditional Access requirement in Entra (SEC-AUTH-02); the application does not inspect amr/acr claims, so it cannot detect a token issued without MFA. See F-G2-08 (medium).

Only three AllowAnonymous groups exist (health probes, /bff/login|signout-entra|maintenance, SPA/404 fallback) and the BI bearer is on its own scheme. But the test that is supposed to prove every endpoint is protected filters on endpoints that carry a perm: policy (AccessAndConcurrencyTests.cs:36-38), so an /api endpoint that forgot RequirePermission is not caught (it would silently fall back to "any authenticated user", as /me/preferences deliberately does).
rows.fix: Extend the test (or add an architecture test) to enumerate /api endpoints with no perm: policy and compare against an explicit allow-list (me/preferences, bff/user).

rows.note: The CRM issues no initial passwords or activation codes; a user row is created on the first Entra sign-in (UserProvisioning). Temporary access passes are an Entra process.
No password hints or knowledge-based questions exist in the application or its UI (no local credentials at all).
The application has no password-reset flow; reset is Entra self-service password reset, whose MFA enforcement is a tenant setting (EXT-02).
Re-enrolment after a lost MFA factor happens in Entra / the IT helpdesk, not in the CRM; the identity-proofing procedure is not documented in the repo.

The application generates no lookup secrets, out-of-band codes or TOTPs; second factors live entirely in Entra. (Case numbers and expected-hash confirmations in the privacy and import flows are not authentication factors.)

Whether SMS/voice OTP is allowed is decided by the Entra authentication-methods policy; the CRM offers no PSTN mechanism itself. The tenant policy cannot be verified from the repo.
The CRM has no out-of-band authentication requests of its own; push/number-matching is Entra Authenticator behaviour.
The CRM has no code-based out-of-band mechanism; brute-force limits on codes are an Entra matter.

Entra is the only IdP; the app registration is single-tenant with assignment required, users are keyed by (tenant id, object id), and BI tokens are checked against the configured tenant. But nothing in code asserts that AzureAd:TenantId is a concrete tenant (appsettings.json ships it empty, a mistaken "common"/"organizations" value would be accepted) and the cookie flow has no test with a real OIDC validation.
rows.fix: At startup in Entra mode, refuse an empty or multi-tenant AzureAd:TenantId (not a GUID / common / organizations / consumers).

rows.note: The id_token of the browser flow is validated by Microsoft.Identity.Web (signature through the tenant JWKS, issuer, audience, nonce, lifetime) and the BI bearer sets RequireSignedTokens/ValidateIssuerSigningKey/ValidateLifetime explicitly; the BI test refuses expired, foreign-tenant, foreign-audience and unsigned tokens. The OIDC part relies on library defaults and has no CRM test.
SAML is not used; the only federation protocol is OIDC with the authorization code flow.

The app does not request or check authentication strength or recentness from Entra (no acr/amr/auth_time/max_age/prompt). "Fresh" for privileged actions means the CRM role confirmation is <5 min old, which a silent SSO sign-in or the 2-minute directory sync satisfies without any user interaction; billing approval and exports therefore get no step-up.
rows.fix: For permissions in Permissions.Privileged, send an authentication-context/claims challenge (or prompt=login&max_age) and verify auth_time/acr in the new ticket before stamping crm_roles_verified; otherwise document the accepted risk in ADR-019.

rows.note: Inactivity (8 h sliding) and absolute (12 h) lifetimes are documented in SEC-AUTH-04 and ADR-019 (item 7, with the rejected 5-minute alternative and its reasoning), set in appsettings and enforced by the cookie ticket and the SessionStarted claim; the absolute limit has an integration test with a manual clock.
No document or code defines how many parallel sessions an account may have: every sign-in adds an UserSessions row and none is ever ended by a newer one.
rows.fix: Document the decision (unlimited with an audit trail is acceptable for an internal CRM) in ADR-019 or add a per-user cap/notification; expose open sessions (see V7.5.2).

rows.note: Entra is the one SSO system and the CRM-to-Entra relationship (hourly refresh-token check, single sign-out, directory sync) is documented, but the Entra-side session policy (sign-in frequency, persistent browser session, token lifetimes) that bounds the whole chain is not documented.
rows.fix: Add the intended Entra Conditional Access session controls (sign-in frequency, persistence) to SEC-AUTH-02 and verify them in the tenant.

rows.note: Every request re-validates the cookie principal on the server: session row open, user active, roles and confirmation time come from the database (replica cache <=30 s); cookie role claims are overwritten. Integration test AC03 shows a copied cookie on a second replica is refused after logout and role removal.

The session token is the ASP.NET Core cookie ticket, encrypted and authenticated by Data Protection (shared Blob + Key Vault key ring, production refuses to start without it) and naming a server session id; no static API key or shared secret is used for user sessions.

The session id is a unique GUID (64 CSPRNG bits + timestamp/counter via SequentialId) but it is never a bearer secret: the value presented by the browser is the Data Protection ciphertext, so guessing a session id has no use. A purely random id would be cleaner, no test of uniqueness.

Each authentication (ProvisionUserAsync) creates a new UserSessions row and the SignIn issues a new cookie, so there is no fixation. The previous session of the same user is not ended: after re-authentication the old cookie value stays valid (until its own expiry) because StartAsync only inserts.
rows.fix: In SessionDirectory.StartAsync end the session named by the incoming cookie (when present) in the same SaveChanges, with reason "Reauthenticated".

rows.note: An 8-hour sliding timeout (ticket renewed only after half the window has passed) is configured and documented with a risk rationale, but it spans a whole working day, effectively never forcing re-authentication in daytime, and no test covers the idle expiry (the lifecycle test only advances the clock for the absolute limit).
rows.fix: Add an integration test that advances beyond SlidingExpiration without activity; consider a shorter idle limit (e.g. 2-4 h) for roles holding Privileged permissions.

rows.note: Absolute lifetime (12 h) is carried in the protected crm_session_started claim and enforced on every request regardless of activity; the integration test proves an active, directory-confirmed session still ends at the absolute limit.

POST /bff/logout closes the UserSessions row and the copied cookie is refused on the local replica at once and on other replicas after at most 30 s (cache TTL, tested in AC03). Paths that end the Entra session do not close the server session: GET /bff/signout-entra only calls Results.SignOut and no front-/back-channel logout handler exists, so a copy of the cookie survives until it expires or the hourly refresh check fails.
rows.fix: Handle OIDC remote sign-out (OnRemoteSignOut) and the signout-entra route by also calling ISessionDirectory.EndAsync for the cookie's sid; make signout-entra a POST or require the CSRF header.

rows.note: A user deactivated by the Entra sync is refused on the next request after the 30 s session-state cache (ActiveUserMiddleware adds a 60 s cache; integration test AC02 shows 401). The sessions are not ended: User.Deactivate() only flips IsActive, and Reactivate() or a later sign-in (RecordSignIn sets IsActive=true) makes old cookies valid again until their 12 h absolute limit.
rows.fix: End all open UserSessions of the user in the same transaction as Deactivate (or handle the UserDeactivated event), so reactivation does not revive old cookies.

rows.note: The CRM manages no authentication factors or passwords: credential changes happen in Entra, and the hourly refresh-token redemption (AuthenticationSetup.cs:224) ends sessions after a password reset or session revocation. There is nothing in the app to offer "end my other sessions" for.

The authenticated shell offers sign-out on every page and the no-access page has it as well; both POST /bff/logout and then follow signOutUrl to Entra. No UI test checks that the control is present on every route.

There is no endpoint or UI for an administrator to end one user's or all sessions (ADR-019 states this explicitly); urgent revocation depends on removing the role/disabling the account in Entra (~2.5 min) and key-ring rotation is deliberately not a revocation tool. A role-less but active user keeps an open session and the read-only shell.
rows.fix: Add POST /api/v1/identity/users/{id}/sessions/end and a global variant (reason, If-Match, audit, privileged permission, ExportsData-style freshness) that call SessionDirectory.EndAsync for open rows; document in runbook 12.

rows.note: The application lets users change no authentication-relevant attribute: names, e-mail and roles come from Entra, /me/preferences changes only the UI language, and there is no role-assignment UI (docs/06-security.md STRIDE table). Such changes require Entra re-authentication in Entra itself.
Sessions are stored (UserSessions) but no API or UI lets a user view or terminate their own active sessions.
rows.fix: Add GET /api/v1/identity/me/sessions and DELETE /me/sessions/{id} (and "end all others") restricted to the caller's rows, plus a SPA account page.

rows.note: Relying-party/IdP coupling is handled by the hourly forced refresh-token redemption (Entra "no" ends the session, outage postpones 5 min; tested in SessionLifecycleTests.cs:274) and by RP-initiated sign-out. The registered logoutUrl /signout-oidc (register-app.sh:48) is the framework front-channel path, which does not close the server session, and no back-channel logout is configured. Entra-side session policy is a tenant matter.
rows.fix: Close the server session from the remote-sign-out event (see V7.4.1) and verify Entra sign-in frequency in the tenant.

rows.note: Creating a session needs a navigation to GET /bff/login, which the SPA triggers automatically on any 401, and the endpoint can be reached by any cross-site link or redirect; with an Entra SSO session the browser then completes sign-in without any click (login CSRF - the attacker gets no session, but the victim gets one unasked). There is no interstitial or consent step.
rows.fix: Show a "Sign in" button on the SPA landing state instead of auto-redirecting after logout, and require a same-site Sec-Fetch-Site (or a CSRF-style state value from the SPA) on /bff/login.

findings.title: Open redirect after sign-in: returnUrl control characters bypass SafeReturnUrl (static analysis, not executed)
findings.description: SafeReturnUrl accepts any string that starts with "/" and not with "//" or "/\". In Entra mode the value becomes AuthenticationProperties.RedirectUri and the OIDC handler issues Response.Redirect(RedirectUri) after sign-in without Url.IsLocalUrl. A value such as "/<TAB>/evil.example" or "/<TAB>\evil.example" starts with "/" followed by a tab, so it passes the check, Kestrel allows HTAB in header values, and browsers strip tabs/newlines when parsing Location, turning it into "//evil.example". Outside the assessed chapters (ASVS V3/V10 redirects) but found while reviewing the login flow. No test covers SafeReturnUrl.
findings.reproduction: Open https://<crm>/bff/login?returnUrl=%2F%09%2Fevil.example while signed out of the CRM; after Entra completes, check whether the final Location resolves to //evil.example. Unit-test SafeReturnUrl("/\t/evil.example") returns the input.
findings.fix: Reject returnUrl containing any control character (char.IsControl), backslash anywhere, or a ":" before the first "/" segment; better, validate with new Uri(returnUrl, UriKind.Relative) and require Path-only; add unit tests for tab, CR, LF, "%09", "/\\".

findings.title: No way to see or end sessions: no admin termination, no per-user session list, no concurrent-session policy
findings.description: identity.UserSessions is written and read only by the sign-in/logout/validation paths. There is no endpoint to end a given user's or all sessions (ADR-019 says so), no self-service list, and no documented rule on parallel sessions. Emergency revocation relies on the directory sync (~2.5 min) and works only by role removal or account disablement.
findings.reproduction: Sign in on two browsers as the same user; log out in one: the other stays valid. As Admin look for an API/UI to end the other: none exists.
findings.fix: Add self-service and administrator session endpoints (audited, privileged freshness) calling SessionDirectory.EndAsync; document the concurrency decision.

findings.title: Old sessions survive re-authentication and deactivation; reactivation revives them
findings.description: SessionDirectory.StartAsync only inserts a row. A new sign-in does not end the session of the cookie it replaces, User.Deactivate() does not end open sessions, and User.RecordSignIn()/Reactivate() set IsActive=true again, so a cookie copied before the deactivation works again if the account is re-enabled within 12 h.
findings.reproduction: Sign in, copy the cookie, deactivate the account via the sync (cookie gets 401), re-enable it in Entra and let the sync run: the copied cookie is accepted again while younger than 12 h.
findings.fix: End open sessions in Deactivate handling and end the replaced session in StartAsync; add integration tests next to SessionLifecycleTests.AC02.

findings.title: Entra-side sign-out routes do not end the server session; GET sign-out is a logout CSRF
findings.description: GET /bff/signout-entra is anonymous, state-changing and only calls Results.SignOut for the OIDC scheme; no OnRemoteSignOut handler or back-channel logout exists, and the registered logoutUrl /signout-oidc is the framework front-channel path. Neither closes identity.UserSessions. Any site can navigate the user to /bff/signout-entra to sign them out of Entra (the Strict cookie is not sent cross-site, but the Entra session is ended).
findings.reproduction: Copy the cookie, call GET /bff/signout-entra (or sign out of Entra elsewhere): the copied cookie still returns 200 on /bff/user until the hourly refresh check or expiry.
findings.fix: Implement OnRemoteSignOut/signout-entra to call ISessionDirectory.EndAsync(sid); make the Entra sign-out a POST with the CSRF header, or add a post-logout state value.

findings.title: CSV imports are unbounded in memory and not documented
findings.description: Four endpoints (licensing import, ms-billing import, price-sheet import, organization migration import and reconcile) read the whole request body into memory and parse it fully before any row cap; only the Kestrel default body limit (~30 MB) applies and no content type is enforced. docs/06-security.md:45 claims a 25 MB limit, signature check and Defender scan that are not implemented.
findings.reproduction: As a user with licensing.manage POST a 28 MB CSV of short lines to /api/v1/licensing/import?dryRun=true several times in parallel and watch crm-web memory (1 GiB container).
findings.fix: Apply an explicit request size limit and row cap (e.g. 5 MB / 20 000 rows) on all four endpoints before parsing, require a text content type, and correct the documentation.

findings.title: HSTS uses framework defaults, contradicting the security specification
findings.description: app.UseHsts() runs without AddHsts, so Strict-Transport-Security is max-age=2592000 without includeSubDomains, while docs/06-security.md:41 requires max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains. No test asserts the header.
findings.fix: Configure HstsOptions (365 days, includeSubDomains) and add an integration test.

findings.title: Forwarded headers trusted from any sender and AllowedHosts "*"
findings.description: KnownIPNetworks and KnownProxies are cleared and XForwardedHost is processed, with AllowedHosts "*". Request.Host (used for OIDC redirect_uri and absolute links) and RemoteIpAddress (used for audit and unauthenticated rate-limit partitions) are therefore only as trustworthy as the ingress is at stripping client-supplied values; not shown in the repo.
findings.reproduction: Send X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example to /bff/login on the test environment and inspect the redirect_uri in the Entra redirect.
findings.fix: Remove XForwardedHost or pin AllowedHosts to the app FQDN through Bicep; add a test.

findings.title: Privileged actions have a role-confirmation freshness but no authentication step-up
findings.description: AUTH_REVERIFY_REQUIRED is satisfied by any sign-in or by the directory sync marking roles confirmed; Entra SSO signs the user in silently and the app never requests or validates acr/amr/auth_time. A stolen or unattended session therefore performs billing approval, exports or maintenance after a silent re-login, and MFA enforcement cannot be seen by the application.
findings.reproduction: With an active Entra SSO session, wait 6 minutes, receive 403 AUTH_REVERIFY_REQUIRED, hit /bff/login: no prompt is shown and the next privileged call succeeds.
findings.fix: Challenge with prompt=login/max_age or an authentication-context claim for Privileged permissions and check auth_time/acr before stamping crm_roles_verified; real MFA enforcement remains EXT-02.

findings.title: The "every endpoint is protected" test skips endpoints without a perm: policy
findings.description: The matrix test keeps only endpoints whose metadata contains a "perm:" policy (.Where(e => e.Policies.Count > 0)). An /api endpoint that omits RequirePermission is authenticated-only through the fallback policy and is not reported, although CLAUDE.md states that a test fails for unprotected endpoints. /api/v1/identity/me/preferences is such an endpoint by design.
findings.reproduction: Add app.MapGet("/api/v1/x", () => 1) without RequirePermission: the test still passes.
findings.fix: Fail the test for any /api endpoint without a perm: policy unless it appears in an explicit allow-list.

findings.title: MSAL token cache (refresh tokens) in SQL uses library defaults
findings.description: AddDistributedTokenCaches() with a SQL Server distributed cache (identity.TokenCache) is configured without MsalDistributedTokenCacheAdapterOptions, i.e. without application-level encryption of the cached refresh tokens (library default Encrypt=false); only TDE protects them from DBAs and from the crm_web role. Not a G2 requirement; reported as an adjacent session-security observation.
findings.reproduction: SELECT TOP 1 * FROM identity.TokenCache as a holder of read rights and inspect the blob.

findings.title: /bff/login creates a session without an explicit user action (login CSRF)
findings.description: GET /bff/login is anonymous, accepts cross-site navigations and, with an Entra SSO session, signs the user in silently; the SPA also redirects to it automatically on every 401 (web/src/api/client.ts:78).
findings.reproduction: From another origin link to https://<crm>/bff/login while the victim has an Entra session: a CRM session starts with no click.
findings.fix: Require a user gesture on the landing page after logout and reject cross-site navigations (Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site) at /bff/login.

findings.title: Entry points under /bff are outside rate limiting; Entra mode not guarded for tenant
findings.description: The global limiter returns NoLimiter for everything except /api, so /bff/login and the OIDC callback have no throttle (each login attempt costs a Challenge and, on callback, user provisioning and a UserSessions insert). There is also no startup assertion that AzureAd:TenantId is a concrete tenant.
findings.reproduction: Loop GET /bff/login 1000 times: no 429 is returned.
findings.fix: Add a per-IP limiter policy on /bff/login and /signin-oidc, and fail startup when AzureAd:TenantId is empty or multi-tenant.

findings.title: Idle timeout of 8 hours is untested and effectively never forces re-authentication
findings.description: Sliding expiration is 8 h (ticket reissued after half the window) and only the absolute limit is covered by SessionLifecycleTests.
findings.reproduction: Advance the test clock by 9 h without requests, expect 401; no such test exists.
findings.fix: Add the idle-expiry test and decide whether privileged roles need a shorter idle limit.
